name: Michael Jordan
summary: 1988 DPOY and All-Defensive 1st Team 1988-89; snubbed 1987 but elite ball-hawk; some modern skeptics of the DPOY.

name: David Robinson
summary: 1992 DPOY; All-Defensive 2nd 1994, 1st 1995; premier shot-blocking, mobile center.

name: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar
summary: Pre-All-Defensive-1st era for him (first honors 1974); dominant length and rim deterrent per retrospectives, but defense less emphasized than scoring; blocks not yet tracked.

name: Magic Johnson
summary: No All-Defensive honors; described as too slow to stay with quick guards (1989 Finals vs Pistons); size and team-defense IQ helped in Dunleavy's defensive 1990-91 scheme.

name: Larry Bird
summary: All-Defensive 2nd 1982-84 but none in 1985-87; smart team/help defender with good hands, limited lateral quickness against quick forwards; mocked by Barkley as poor defender.

name: Hakeem Olajuwon
summary: DPOY 1993 and 1994; All-Defensive 1st; MVP/DPOY/FMVP 1994; trophy now named for him.

name: Scottie Pippen
summary: All-Defensive 1st Team 1994-96 (8 straight); long arms, quick feet, guarded every position.

name: John Stockton
summary: All-Defensive 2nd Team 1991, 1992; steals leader 1992; pesky, physical, smart; size limits.

name: Oscar Robertson
summary: No All-Defensive teams yet; sources mention toughness and tenacious, physical defense but reputation is overwhelmingly offensive.

name: Charles Barkley
summary: Never All-Defensive; widely viewed as inconsistent/low-effort defender relying on rebounding and occasional blocks/steals; discipline issues 1989-90.

name: Jerry West
summary: Pre-All-Defensive era; later 5 straight All-Defensive selections from 1969; NBA profile cites tenacious defense, quick hands.

name: Karl Malone
summary: No All-Defensive honors 1992-94 (2nd 1988, 1st 1997-99); strong, physical post defender and good team defender, though not yet honored in this window.

name: Bill Russell
summary: Consensus greatest defender ever; Wooden: 'greatest defensive man I've ever seen'; shot-blocking/tip-blocking anchor of Celtics dynasty.

name: Wilt Chamberlain
summary: Hannum refocused him on defense/rebounding in 1967 title season; dominant shot blocker (6 blocks in 4th qtr of clinching Finals game).

name: Walt Frazier
summary: All-Defensive 1st Team 1969-75 including all three seasons; famed quick hands and steals.

name: Moses Malone
summary: All-Defensive 1st Team 1983 (only first-team nod), 2nd 1979; strong rebounding/positional defender, less noted as rim protector in 1981-82.

name: Clyde Drexler
summary: Never All-Defensive; high steal totals and 8th in 1988 DPOY voting, but reputation as gambling, offense-first defender.

name: Patrick Ewing
summary: All-Defensive 2nd Team 1988 and 1989; elite shot blocker (3+ bpg).

name: Julius Erving
summary: Ranked among Sixers' top defenders; credited for help-side blocks and steals; no All-Defensive in window.

name: Bill Walton
summary: All-Defensive 1st Team 1977 and 1978; led league in blocks 1977; anchor of title team.

name: Gary Payton
summary: 'The Glove'; All-Defensive 1st 1994-96; 1996 DPOY, first PG to win.

name: John Havlicek
summary: All-Defensive 1st Team 1972 (and 2nd 1970-71 era); relentless, tireless two-way wing.

name: Isiah Thomas
summary: High steals (2.5 spg 1984) and intensity, but no All-Defensive; noted gambler, coach wanted more defense.

name: Rick Barry
summary: Led NBA in steals 1975, played passing lanes superbly, but defense sometimes criticized as less than intense; no All-Defensive.

name: Anfernee Hardaway
summary: Long-armed, versatile; SI: often guarded forwards; solid defense on Jordan; no All-Defensive.

name: Kevin Johnson
summary: No All-Defensive; decent steals, quick; sources focus on offense; defense not specifically praised or criticized.

name: Bob McAdoo
summary: Shot blocker (3.3 bpg 1974) per SI, but Braves were last in team defense; considered offense-first.

name: Chris Mullin
summary: Below-average athlete on a Run TMC team with bottom-tier defense; decent hands but generally regarded as a defensive weak link.

name: Reggie Miller
summary: Mixed: coach called him underrated defender who drew top scorers; SI noted liabilities as defender; slight frame.

name: George Gervin
summary: SI 1978: defense a 'mere bagatelle' for Spurs; scorer reputation; some opponents called him underrated.
